text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - A five-day strike by Czech rail caused losses at Slovak Railways (ZRS) of some 1.4 million crowns. ZRS will also have to pay 2.1 million crowns for each day of the strike to neighbouring railway operators for international trains going through Slovakia during the strike.
- U.S.-Slovak GSM operator Eurotel on Monday launches commercial operation of its network.
- The World Bank, International Finance Corporation and the Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency on Monday open a two-day conference on the Slovak entrepreneur sector.

- Chemical company Chemosvit Svit expects to post a pre-tax profit of around 140 million crowns in 1996 on production totalling 3.3 billion crowns. Chemosvit said it planned to invest about 600 million crowns in modernisation projects this year.
- Average industrial nominal wages rose 14.6 percent year-on-year, by 16.4 percent in construction sector and by 14.7 percent in transport sector.

NARODNA OBRODA - Parliament has approved two candidates for the one vacant seat at the Constitutional Court. Both Jan Cuper and Lubomir Dobrik are members of the ruling Movement for a Democratic Slovakia (HZDS). A new member of the court will be chosen by President Michal Kovac.
- The ultra-left Workers Party (ZRS), a junior member of the ruling coalition, said it would not join any coalition in the 1998 election campaign.
- Engineering company ZOS Vrutky, specialising in the production and modernisation of railway equipment, has been awarded an international quality certificate by Det Norske Veritas.

- Hygienic paper producer SCA Molnlycke Gemerska Horka, wholly-owned by Sweden's SCA Molnlycke, expects to post gross profit of around 100 million crowns in 1996, up from 38 million in the previous year.
- Private Slovak airline Tatra Air said it would inaugurate a bi-weekly route between Bratislava and Kiev in May.
SME - Steel producer VSZ said it had to reduce its main steel production last weekend due to an interruption in coal supplies caused by the strike of Czech railway workers.
